headline: PM chairs meeting on Dhaka's public transport management
summary: The meeting focused on ensuring road safety and eliminating chaos in the capital's public transport system.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman chaired a high-level meeting on Thursday to discuss the management of public transport in Dhaka city.
The meeting took place at the the Cabinet Division of the Bangladesh Secretariat.
The primary goals discussed were improving public transport management, ensuring road safety, and eliminating existing chaos in the system.
Key attendees included Road Transport and Bridges Minister Sheikh Rabiul Alam, State Ministers for Road Transport and Bridges and Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives.

Other high-ranking officials present included the Prime Minister's Chief Secretary, the Secretary of the Local Government Division, and the Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA) Executive Director.
The meeting also included the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner, and the Secretary of the Road Transport and Highways Division.
The discussions aimed to create a more structured and safer transport environment for the residents of Dhaka.

headline_marked: 2 days after restart, [[Jamuna Fertilizer plant shuts down]] again
headline: 2 days after restart, Jamuna Fertilizer plant shuts down again
summary: Production stopped due to a technical fault in a plant boiler after the factory had resumed full operations following an 8-month gas crisis.
details: The Jamuna Fertilizer Company Limited (JFCL) in Sarishabari, Jamalpur, has halted production just two days after resuming full operations.
General Manager (Operations) Md. Fazlul Haque confirmed that a leak was discovered in a plant boiler around 3:30 AM on Wednesday, necessitating an immediate shutdown for repairs.
The management described the issue as a minor technical fault and stated that repairs are underway to prevent any larger problems in the future.
The factory is expected to return to full production by Saturday. The GM noted that small issues are common when a plant restarts after a long hiatus.
The plant had previously shut down on February 15 this year due to a severe gas crisis and only resumed full operations last Monday night.
Currently, with the available gas pressure, the factory is capable of producing approximately 1,300 metric tons of urea daily, which could increase to 1,400 metric tons if pressure improves.
Established in 1991 with a daily capacity of 1,700 tons, the Jamuna Fertilizer plant supplies urea to 19 districts, including 16 in the northern region of Bangladesh.
caption:
After an 8-month gas crisis, the Jamuna Fertilizer plant restarted—only to shut down again in 48 hours.

The Jamuna Fertilizer Company Limited (JFCL) in Sarishabari, Jamalpur, has halted production just two days after resuming full operations.

General Manager (Operations) Md. Fazlul Haque confirmed that a leak was discovered in a plant boiler around 3:30 AM on Wednesday, necessitating an immediate shutdown for repairs.

The management described the issue as a minor technical fault and stated that repairs are underway to prevent any larger problems in the future.

The factory is expected to return to full production by Saturday. The GM noted that small issues are common when a plant restarts after a long hiatus.

The plant had previously shut down on February 15 this year due to a severe gas crisis and only resumed full operations last Monday night.

Currently, with the available gas pressure, the factory is capable of producing approximately 1,300 metric tons of urea daily, which could increase to 1,400 metric tons if pressure improves.

Established in 1991 with a daily capacity of 1,700 tons, the Jamuna Fertilizer plant supplies urea to 19 districts, including 16 in the northern region of Bangladesh.
